arcada: Arcas, -adis (m.) — an Arcadian (acc. sg., Greek form in -a)
archetium: Archetius, -ī (m.) — Archetius, a warrior killed by Mnestheus (acc. sg.)
ars: ars, artis (f.) — skill, craft, trade, occupation (nom. sg.)

cethegum: Cethēgus, -ī (m.) — Cethegus, a warrior killed by Aeneas (acc. sg.)

congressu: congressus, -ūs (m.) — meeting, encounter, clash of combat (abl. sg.)

currunt: currō, -ere, cucurrī, cursum — to run, rush, flow (3rd pl. pres.)
decursu: dēcursus, -ūs (m.) — running down, descent, rush downhill (abl. sg.)

dioren: Diōrēs, -is (m.) — Diores, brother of Amycus, killed by Turnus (acc. sg., Greek form -ēn)
disiecta: disiciō, -ere, -iēcī, -iectum — to scatter, break up, disperse (perf. pass. part., n. acc. pl., with agmina)

diversas: dīversus, -a, -um — turned different ways, scattered, various (f. acc. pl., with caedes)
diversis: dīversus, -a, -um — turned different ways, scattered, separate (f. abl. pl., with partibus)
echionium: Echionius, -a, -um — of Echion, Echionian (n. acc. sg., with nōmen)
epulonem: Epulō, -ōnis (m.) — Epulo, a warrior killed by Achates (acc. sg.)
excutit: excutiō, -ere, -cussī, -cussum — to shake out, knock out, hurl out, dislodge (3rd sg. pres.)
exosum: exōsus, -a, -um — hating, detesting (+ acc.) (m. acc. sg.; active sense, from exōdī)
expediat: expediō, -īre, -īvī, -ītum — to disentangle, set out, unfold, tell (3rd sg. pres. subj., deliberative)
frementi: fremō, -ere, -uī, -itum — to roar, rage, growl (pres. part., m. dat. sg.)
futuras: sum, esse, fuī — to be; futūrus, -a, -um, about to be (fut. part., f. acc. pl., with gentis)
horrescunt: horrescō, -ere, horruī — to bristle, shudder, begin to tremble (3rd pl. pres.)
hyllo: Hyllus, -ī (m.) — Hyllus, a warrior killed by Turnus (dat. sg., with occurrit)
incita: incitō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to urge on, spur, hurl (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; also incitus, hurried, swift)

legens: legō, -ere, lēgī, lēctum — to gather, pick up, collect (pres. part., f. nom. sg.)
loquacibus: loquāx, -ācis — talkative, chattering (m. abl./dat. pl., with nīdīs)
lyrnesi: Lyrnēsus, -ī (f.) — Lyrnesus, a town (gen. sg., 'of Lyrnesus'; or loc. sg., 'at Lyrnesus')
memorum: memor, -oris — mindful, remembering (+ gen.) (m. gen. pl., = memorum for -ium, with equōrum)
metae: mēta, -ae (f.) — turning-post, goal, limit, end (nom. pl.)
missos: mittō, -ere, mīsī, missum — to send (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl., with fratrēs)
mnestheusque: Mnestheus, -eī (m.) — Mnestheus, a warrior on Aeneas's side (nom. sg., Greek form) + -que 'and'
murranum: Murrānus, -ī (m.) — Murranus, a man of Latin royal descent, killed by Aeneas (acc. sg.)
obitumque: obitus, -ūs (m.) — going down, death, end (acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
occidis: occidō, -ere, -cidī, -cāsum — to fall, die, be killed (2nd sg. pres.)
oniten: Onītēs, -ae (m.) — Onites, son of Peridia, killed by Aeneas (acc. sg., Greek form -ēn)
osirim: Osīris, -is (m.) — Osiris, a warrior killed by Thymbraeus (acc. sg., Greek form -im)
peridiae: Perīdia, -ae (f.) — Peridia, mother of Onites (gen. sg.)
pervolat: pervolō, -āre — to fly through, flit all over (3rd sg. pres.)
piscosae: piscōsus, -a, -um — full of fish, teeming with fish (f. gen. sg., with Lernae)
placuit: placeō, -ēre, -uī, -itum — to please, be pleasing (+ dat.) (3rd sg. perf., used impersonally)
populatus: populor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to ravage, lay waste (perf. part. of deponent, m. nom. sg., active sense)
potentum: potēns, -entis — powerful; as noun, the powerful (m. gen. pl., = potentium)
proculcat: proculcō, -āre — to trample down, tread underfoot (3rd sg. pres.)
provolvere: prōvolvō, -ere, -volvī, -volūtum — to roll forward, roll over (3rd pl. perf., = prōvolvērunt)
rapidoque: rapidus, -a, -um — swift, rushing (m. abl. sg., with currū) + -que 'and'
retorsit: retorqueō, -ēre, -torsī, -tortum — to twist back, turn back (3rd sg. perf.)
rhoeteius: Rhoetēius, -a, -um — of Rhoeteum, a headland of the Troad; hence Trojan (m. nom. sg., with ductor)
ruenti: ruō, -ere, ruī — to rush, charge, fall headlong (pres. part., m. dat. sg.)
ruet: ruō, -ere, ruī — to rush, tumble; trans., to bring down, overthrow (3rd sg. fut.)
rumpuntur: rumpō, -ere, rūpī, ruptum — to break, burst (3rd pl. pres. pass.)
saevam: saevus, -a, -um — savage, fierce, raging (f. acc. sg., with caedem)
segnius: sēgnis, -e — slow, sluggish; comp. adv. sēgnius, more slowly (non segnius, no less keenly)
sepulchrum: sepulchrum, -ī (n.) — tomb, burial place (nom. sg.; also acc. sg.)
serebat: serō, -ere, sēvī, satum — to sow, plant, till (3rd sg. impf.)
spumosi: spūmōsus, -a, -um — foamy, frothing (m. nom. pl., with amnēs)
subactus: subigō, -ere, -ēgī, -āctum — to subdue, overcome, drive under (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
subsidens: subsīdō, -ere, -sēdī — to sink down, crouch, settle (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
sucronem: Sucrō, -ōnis (m.) — Sucro, a Rutulian, killed by Aeneas (acc. sg.)
summasque: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost (f. acc. pl., with cristās) + -que 'and'
talon: Talos, -ī (m.) — Talos, a warrior killed by Aeneas (acc. sg., Greek form -on)
tanaimque: Tanaīs, -is (m.) — Tanais, a warrior killed by Aeneas (acc. sg., Greek form -im) + -que 'and'
temptavit: temptō (tentō), -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to try, attempt, test (3rd sg. perf.)
thymbraeus: Thymbraeus, -ī (m.) — Thymbraeus, a warrior on Aeneas's side (nom. sg.)
torserat: torqueō, -ēre, torsī, tortum — to twist, whirl, hurl (3rd sg. plupf.)
tortos: torqueō, -ēre, torsī, tortum — to twist; tortus, twisted, winding (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl., with orbēs)
totae: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (f. nom. pl., with aciēs)
ufentemque: Ūfēns, -entis (m.) — Ufens, a warrior killed by Gyas (acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
vestigat: vestīgō, -āre — to track, trace, hunt out (3rd sg. pres.)
vestigatque: vestīgō, -āre — to track, trace, hunt out (3rd sg. pres.) + -que 'and'
vicem: vicis (gen.), vicem, vice — turn, change, place (acc. sg.; inque vicem, 'in turn')
vinci: vincō, -ere, vīcī, victum — to conquer, defeat (pres. inf. pass.; nescia vinci, 'not knowing how to be beaten')
